THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 07.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:12901 MACA NO. 1174 OF 2014  3  JUDGMENT

The 3rd respondent in OP(MV) 846/2003 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Mavelikara is the appellant herein.

The original petitioners are the wife, minor children and mother of Gopinathan Nair, who died in an accident on 28.11.2002 (For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2.

According to the petitioners, on 28.11.2002 at about 6:15 p.m, while the deceased was standing at the south-east side of the waiting shed at Kochalummoodu Junction in the Manakamkuxhi- Kollakadavu public road, a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-2H-7447 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit him down and as a result of which, he sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
The 3 rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The evidence in the case consists of oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A8.
4. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.13,04,100/-.

sentences.text: 5. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the 3rd respondent preferred this appeal.

6. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

7. Heard Sri.Arun Bose, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellants, and Sri.George Cherian,
learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
8.
The points:
The main contention raised by the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant is that, though the salary of the deceased on the date of the accident was only 4,309/-.
The tribunal has taken his notional income as Rs.10,000/- on the ground that, at the time of passing the award, the salary of a Lower Division Clerk was about 13,000/-.
According to him, the above procedure adopted by the Tribunal was against the evidence on record.
The learned counsel for the petitioners attempted to show that the Court could take note of the subsequent development.

In a proceeding under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation on account of the death of a victim, what is to be looked into is the income of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
In this case the deceased was a Higher Secondary LD Clerk and his salary on the date of the accident as revealed from Ext.A8 Salary Certificate is only Rs.4,309/-.
In the above circumstances, the Tribunal was not justified in taking judicial notice of subsequent developments and subsequent pay.
In the above circumstances, the income of the deceased on the date of the accident is liable to be fixed as Rs.4,309/-.

10. Since, the deceased was aged 38 on the date of the accident and he was on a permanent employment, 50% of the income is directed to be added towards future prospects and the multiplier to be applied is 15.
Since, he had four dependents 1/4 of the income is liable to be deducted towards personal and living expense.
Therefore, loss of dependency will come to Rs.8,72,572/-.

11. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/-
towards funeral expense, Rs.10,000/- was awarded towards the head of pain and suffering and towards the head loss of consortium Rs.15,000/- was awarded, which 2025:KER:12901 MACA NO.
1174 OF 2014 according to him are on the lower side.
At the same time, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- on the head of loss of love and affection.

12. In the light of the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680], the appellants are entitled to a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses, Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% for every three years.
